sentences.text:
Author: Deepak Verma
Bench: Deepak Verma

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 78 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 55506 of 2022 Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Yogesh Kumar Tiwari

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,M.P.S. Chauhan Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
Second supplementary affidavit, filed today by learned counsel for the applicant, is taken on record.
Counter affidavit, filed by learned counsel for the informant, is also taken on record.

Heard Sri Y.K. Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri M.P.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant Rakesh Kumar with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 85 of 2022, u/s 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., P.S. Godha,
District Aligarh during pendency of the trial.
It is alleged in the FIR that the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) was approved in favour of the informant in the year 2019, thereafter, applicant transferred amount of Rs.2,90,000/- in his own account.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case due to prior enmity.
The KCC amount was transferred in the account of informant.
Thereafter, the applicant put the cheque which was given by the informant to him for borrowed money, therefore, he withdrew the amount from the account of the informant.
It is further submitted that the applicant has criminal history of one case.
There is no prospect of trial of the present case being concluded in near future due to heavy dockets.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 9.10.2022 and in case he is enlarged on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer of the applicant and urged that the informant had issued blank cheque in favour of the applicant for processing cash credit card but the applicant misused the same.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another, passed in S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Rakesh Kumar, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/ pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
